title: Lock the meme. Earn its pair.
blocks: Every memecoin has one recurring revenue stream: the fee people pay to trade it. On most launchpads that fee goes to the platform and the creator, and none of it to the people whose holding is the reason there is a price at all. IMAGINE changes where it lands. The site is imagine.fun.

If the only action that pays a holder is selling, everybody sells, and the chart looks like it. IMAGINE pays the other action. Every trade on an IMAGINE coin pays a fee into that coin's pool, and the pool pays the holders who locked it, weighted by how long each of them committed.
Paired with anything, paid in its pair

IMAGINE coins launch on StonkFun, the Solana launchpad where every coin is paired with an asset: a tokenized stock such as NVDAx, SPYx or TSLAx, a stablecoin, or SOL. The coin is created on StonkFun's Raydium LaunchLab platform like any other StonkFun coin, trades on the same curve, and shows up in the same places.

Because the coin trades against its pair, the fees are in its pair, and so are the rewards. A coin paired with NVDAx pays its lockers NVDAx. A SOL-paired coin pays SOL. A USDC-paired coin pays USDC. Lock the meme; earn its pair.

Two streams land in one vault per coin, both in the pair asset. First, imagine.fun adds a 1% app fee on trades it routes, paid into that coin's pool inside the swap transaction: if the trade fails, no fee is taken; if it lands, the fee is already in the pool. Second, StonkFun charges 1% on curve trades and forwards a creator share to the coin's creator address. For an IMAGINE coin, that creator address is the pool's vault, so whatever StonkFun forwards arrives where the lockers are paid from. How much it forwards, and when, is StonkFun's policy; IMAGINE counts what arrives.

The pool splits what it receives one way, frozen at launch: 90% to the people who locked, by weight, and 10% to the treasury. The creator's share is zero by default. A creator earns the way everyone else does, by locking, and their founding lock opens in the same transaction that launches the coin.
Locking, and why the curve bends

You lock for a term you choose, from four hours to a year. Your share of what arrives is your weight over the pool's total weight, and weight is amount times a multiplier on a square-root curve: four hours counts once, a day 1.14×, a week 1.41×, a month 1.86×, ninety days 2.49×, six months 3.11×, a year 4×. Short locks still count; a long one still takes the top.

Size matters too. Lock a tenth of a percent of the supply and your weight gets 10% more; half a percent, 25%; a full percent, 50%. Size is measured against total supply, so nobody else's lock can move yours.

Fees do not land on lockers the instant they arrive. They stream in over an hour, so a share is earned by holding through time, not by locking a large bag the second before a payout and leaving the second after. Claiming never touches your lock, and your lock never blocks a claim.

You can always break a lock. Selling is free; it just costs you the stream. Your unclaimed rewards go back into the pool for the people who stayed, and a slice of your principal is burned, scaled by how much of your term you did not serve. If you were never going to hold, do not lock. If you were, this pays you for the holding you were already doing.
"Trust us" is not a security model, so the parts that matter are properties of the program, checkable against the source.
There is no admin withdraw path. No instruction moves a pool's funds or locked coins to an admin. Not disabled, not timelocked: absent.

A pool's terms are frozen at launch: the fee split, the multiplier curve, the size tiers, the lock bounds, the early-exit penalty and the treasury address. Defaults can change for future coins, never for yours.
Claims and unlocks cannot be paused. The pause switch stops new launches and nothing else.
The creator locks first. Nobody can lock into a pool before the creator's founding lock exists.

The source, the tests and the security review are linked from imagine.fun/docs/security, which walks through each claim, including the ones that depend on others: StonkFun's forwarding is its own off-chain policy, and tokenized stocks carry their issuer's controls.

Most people who would lock a coin do not have a Solana wallet. IMAGINE takes a Google sign-in: you get an ordinary Solana address, held for you, that you can fund, lock from, claim to, and withdraw from or export whenever you want.

None of this makes a bad coin good. A coin nobody trades pays nothing, and a locked bag in a coin going to zero is worse than an unlocked one, because you cannot sell into the decline for free. Every rate on the site is trailing, realised fees over locked value; nothing is projected, and nothing is promised.
What IMAGINE changes is narrow: the person who stays is the person who gets paid, in whatever the coin is paired with. Imagine the chart if nobody sold.
